etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English obsequyous, from Latin obsequiōsus (“complaisant, obsequious”), from obsequium (“compliance”), from obsequor (“comply with, yield to”), from ob (“in the direction of, towards”) + sequor (“follow”) (cf. sequel).
senses: Excessively eager and attentive to please or to obey instructions; fawning, subservient, servile.
(archaic) Obedient; compliant with someone else's orders or wishes.
